title: Making European friends and the 1969 Monestier tour
summary: His 1948 trip made contacts such as Panassie and Delaunay, and in 1969 he replaces Louis Jordan on a tour with drummer Candy MacDonald.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You know, speaking of going to Europe and of my trip to Europe that time, when I accidentally went over in 1948 instead of Willie, I made a lot of friends. I made friends with Panassié, Charles Delaunay, Curt Moore , Jack Dimitri. I met was not on the scene, this guy who...Jack Morgantini. Those days Monestier / the one who had the Hot Clubs promoting concerts and you had to make contacts with him.

But later on, as the years went by, I made contact...somebody wrote me a letter, said that this guy Jean Maurice Monestier was trying to reach me because Louis Jordan had signed for some dates and that he had not come to fulfill these engagements. And this had caused, you know, quite a problem...the promoters lost a lot of money. So they wanted somebody to come...and this was in '69 when I first started doing these things for Monestier.

So they wanted somebody to come to Europe that could fulfill the engagements and appease the impresarios. So I took the thing and I took Candy MacDonald, a drummer. It was really a whirlwind thing because I met Candy MacDonald at 12 o'clock during the day. He did not have a passport. The drums were put away for safekeeping in a pawn shop. We had to go get his drums out of pawn; go the the State Department and get a passport; I had to go to Air India and get the tickets; had to be at the airport at 7 o'clock. And we accomplished all of this. And when we got to Paris we went on to Bordeaux to meet Menestier and then we started the tour. And we played in a lot of cities and enjoyed a big success, and in St. Etienne--that's a town where the youth have quite a bit to say/ about... we played this big concert and it was a big success. And then I came on back to the States. Now that was the beginning of my going to Europe quite a bit.
